$comment: A REGRESSION FIXTURE, not a known-answer test.
The expected bytes were produced by this implementation, so they prove nothing about
the correctness of AES-CCM -- that is what test-vectors/aes_ccm_rfc3610.json is for,
and RFC 3610 carries no vectors with a 4-byte tag.
What this pins is the FRAME CONSTRUCTION around the cipher: the nonce layout, the
choice of the 12-byte header as AAD, and the truncation of the tag to 4 bytes. Any of
those changing is a wire format change, and docs/versioning-and-updates.md 1 requires a
`ver` bump and both nodes flashed in one session. A silent change here would produce
two nodes that cannot hear each other and a MIC failure indistinguishable from a wrong
key -- which is exactly the evening that document exists to save.

nonce.note: derived, not transmitted: src little endian, then counter little endian, then seven zero bytes

vectors.name: frame_ccm_regression
vectors.note: ciphertext (12 bytes) followed by the 4-byte MIC
